tip: Mynd i'r afael â is a fixed phrase for tackling a task. The â on the end literally means with.
Aches and pains take ar (on), not a verb for have. Arna i means on me, so cur pen arna i is a headache on me.
dy (your) triggers a soft mutation, so pen (head) becomes ben in dy ben.
pont (bridge) is feminine, so it soft-mutates to bont after the article: Mae'r bont.
After a number the noun stays singular: deuddeg mis is twelve month, not months.
ein (our) adds an h before a vowel, so iechyd (health) becomes hiechyd in ein hiechyd.
neu (or) triggers a soft mutation, so pensil becomes bensil in neu bensil.
Gan fod means because or since. It combines gan with fod, a form of bod (to be).
The -wyd ending makes a passive, so Paratowyd means was prepared. The doer follows gan (by): gan y plant.
Welsh has no verb for have. Mae gen i is literally there is with me, so Mae gen i ewythr is I have an uncle.
Heb (without) triggers a soft mutation, so gwybod (to know) becomes wybod in Heb wybod.
cystal â means as good as. The â triggers an aspirate mutation, so cawl becomes chawl after it.
Edrychwn ymlaen at is the set phrase for look forward to. It takes at, not i, before what you await.
a (and) triggers an aspirate mutation, so cig (meat) becomes chig in a chig moch.
